facts.text: Transferable on-road false-activation tests for heavy off-road machines include trench-plate and pass-through equivalents for berms, windrows, dust plumes, parked machines and overhead structures.
facts.quote: Explicit false-activation tests: trench-plate and pass-through equivalents for berms, windrows, dust plumes, parked machines and overhead structures. [38, 39]

facts.text: Machine-independent physical outcome measures for collision-mitigation acceptance include no-contact, residual impact speed, remaining distance, time-to-collision at warning and at brake, and false-reaction outcomes.
facts.quote: Outcome measures that are machine-independent physical quantities: no-contact, residual impact speed, remaining distance, time-to-collision at warning and at brake, and false-reaction outcomes

facts.text: Euro NCAP's virtual protocol compares no-contact, residual impact speed, remaining distance, time-to-collision at warning and at brake, and false-reaction outcomes between physical and simulated runs.
facts.quote: no-contact, residual impact speed, remaining distance, time-to-collision at warning and at brake, and false-reaction outcomes; Euro NCAP's virtual protocol compares exactly these between physical and simulated runs.

facts.text: Impact-speed or stop-gap acceptance tables organized by speed band are a potentially transferable on-road acceptance method for heavy off-road machines.
facts.quote: Impact-speed or stop-gap acceptance tables by speed band. [39]

facts.text: The toolchain credibility frameworks in UN R171 Annex 5 and NATM, together with predicted performance plus random physical verification, map directly onto variant management across machine models.
facts.quote: Toolchain credibility frameworks (R171 Annex 5, NATM) and the predicted-performance-plus-random-physical-verification structure, which maps directly onto variant management across machine models

facts.text: Transferring on-road credibility frameworks to machine variants calls for separate qualification of the vehicle dynamics and brake model, the object and sensor model, and the perception and decision model.
facts.quote: qualify the vehicle dynamics and brake model, the object and sensor model, and the perception and decision model separately

facts.text: Virtual evidence for machine variants should be allowed only inside the validated envelope.
facts.quote: allow virtual evidence only inside the validated envelope

facts.text: A predicted-performance-plus-physical-verification approach for machine variants should include randomly selected physical challenge tests.
facts.quote: run randomly selected physical challenge tests

facts.text: Machine variants should be requalified after material software, sensor-position or machine changes.
facts.quote: requalify after material software, sensor-position or machine changes. [32, 33, 34]

facts.text: Road geometry, lane markings, traffic rules and driver assumptions are unlikely to transfer to off-road collision-mitigation acceptance because mines use haul-road rules, berms and site-specific right-of-way.
facts.quote: Road geometry, lane markings, traffic rules and driver assumptions: mines use haul-road rules, berms and site-specific right-of-way.

facts.text: An articulated dump truck reversing at a crusher, an excavator swinging beside a worker, a loader approaching a stockpile and a haul truck descending a grade have different collision kinematics from on-road rear-end and crossing-pedestrian tests.
facts.quote: An articulated dump truck reversing at a crusher, an excavator swinging beside a worker, a loader approaching a stockpile and a haul truck descending a grade have different collision kinematics from rear-end and crossing-pedestrian tests

facts.text: ISO 21815's separate parts for forward/reverse, swing and other motions support the conclusion that off-road motion types need different hazard models.
facts.quote: ISO 21815's separate parts for forward/reverse, swing and other motions are themselves evidence that off-road motion types need different hazard models. [4, 5]

facts.text: Using only car and pedestrian targets is unlikely to transfer adequately to off-road collision-mitigation acceptance.
facts.quote: Car and pedestrian targets alone, and road speed ranges

facts.text: Road speed ranges are unlikely to transfer to off-road acceptance: off-road speeds are mostly below 60 km/h, while machine masses reach hundreds of tonnes.
facts.quote: Car and pedestrian targets alone, and road speed ranges: off-road speeds are mostly below 60 km/h but masses reach hundreds of tonnes.

facts.text: Dry, flat asphalt surfaces and comfort-oriented deceleration assumptions are unlikely to transfer to heavy off-road machine acceptance.
facts.quote: Dry, flat asphalt surfaces and comfort-oriented deceleration assumptions

facts.text: Gravel, mud, ice, grades of 10% or more, brake temperature, tyre or track interaction, payload transfer, articulated stability and rollover make ISO 3450 more relevant to off-road braking acceptance than imported passenger-car deceleration targets.
facts.quote: gravel, mud, ice, grades of 10% or more, brake temperature, tyre or track interaction, payload transfer, articulated stability and rollover make ISO 3450 more relevant than any imported passenger-car deceleration target. [49]

facts.text: Articulated steering, attachments and raised bodies change machine footprints and are off-road considerations that limit transfer of on-road acceptance assumptions.
facts.quote: Articulated steering, attachments and raised bodies that change the footprint

facts.text: Brake thermal limits and retarders are off-road considerations that limit transfer of on-road acceptance assumptions.
facts.quote: brake thermal limits and retarders

facts.text: Dust, vibration and lens contamination are off-road considerations that limit transfer of on-road acceptance assumptions.
facts.quote: dust, vibration and lens contamination.

facts.text: A virtual method that may assume perfect perception cannot establish that a camera works in airborne dust or glare; separate sensor and perception qualification is needed.
facts.quote: a virtual method that may assume perfect perception cannot establish that a camera works in airborne dust or glare

facts.text: A virtual method that may assume perfect perception cannot establish that lidar remains adequate in heavy precipitation; separate sensor and perception qualification is needed.
facts.quote: that lidar remains adequate in heavy precipitation

facts.text: A virtual method that may assume perfect perception cannot establish that radar resolves a worker next to a large metal structure; separate sensor and perception qualification is needed.
facts.quote: that radar resolves a worker next to a large metal structure; those need separate sensor and perception qualification. [34]

facts.text: The on-road vehicle type-approval regime is unlikely to transfer to off-road acceptance, which relies on manufacturer self-declaration, notified bodies or site acceptance rather than vehicle type approval.
facts.quote: The type-approval regime itself: off-road relies on manufacturer self-declaration, notified bodies or site acceptance, not vehicle type approval.
